(1) the density of cells in the ependyme and the spinal cord of turtles increases with temperature, (2) the density of BrdU-LC in the forebrain of turtles is higher at warm temperature than at cold temperatures, (3) BrdU-LCS are not only glial but may also be non-neuronal and neuronal, and (4) temperature affects the proliferation of non-neuronal cells in the turtle CNS.
the cell proliferation rate in the CNS of juvenile turtles is higher in warm-acclimated animals than in cold-acclimated animals.
the cell proliferation rate in the spinal cord gray matter and in all the brain regions analyzed is increased in turtles acclimated at warm temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of environmental temperature on the cell proliferation rate in the CNS of juvenile turtles.

the effect of environmental temperature (warm versus cold acclimation) on the proliferation rate of cells in the spinal cord (including the ependyma) and in the brain of juvenile turtles, and also with the effect of the light-dark daily cycle (independently from temperature) on cell proliferation.

the effects of environmental temperature on the proliferation rate of cells in the CNS of juvenile turtles, and the possible role that temperature may play in the regulation of cell proliferation in the vertebrate CNS.

temperature affects cell proliferation rate in the CNS of juvenile turtles, and that these effects are independent of light-dark rhythms and are not restricted to glial cells.
